transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-25 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration approx 42m
Attendees: Samir Patel (AE), Rosa Kim (SE) — Redwood; Lena Ortiz (Head of AI), Marcus Hale (Eng Mgr), Dr. Priya Anand (Clinical Safety), Evan Chu (SRE) — Veridion Health

Summary:
Quick failure-mode drill + scorecard calibration. Walked through latest scorecard (precision/recall/FPR) on 1k sample, ran through a simulated fallback/rollback scenario on staging. Decided to tighten guardrail thresholds for clinical-NER outputs, increase negative-sample weighting in scoring, and run a 2k eval before next sync. Agreed on next steps and owners.

Topics covered: scorecard regression, prompt set pruning, guardrail rule tuning, fallback/rollback simulation, dedicated vs hosted routing for high-risk traffic, audit log needs.

Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-transcript imperfect, speakers sometimes generic):
[00:00] Samir: all right folks, thanks for joining, we have about 40 minutes — quick intro, Rosa and I from Redwood, we'll kick off with the scorecard updates.
[00:18] Lena: hi, thanks, yeah quick note, Priya's gonna flag any clinical safety hits, Marcus will handle infra questions, Evan on logs.
[00:29] Rosa: cool, I'll share my screen with the new scoring sheet — if you don't see it ping me in chat. (audio: screen switch)
[00:43] Speaker 1: okay I can see a table, precision, recall, fpr columns, um some rows for prompt variants.
[00:51] Rosa: yeah so top line, variant v1.1-q2 we've got precision 0.86 recall 0.79 fpr 0.12 on the 1k set — there was a cluster of short-prompt missclassifications on medications.
[01:10] Marcus: when you say "fpr 0.12" is that per-case or per-entity? I thought we were scoring per-entity for NER.
[01:17] Rosa: good call — per-entity. We should probably call that out in the header, transcript sometimes shows metric as F P R per case, but it's entity-level.
[01:30] Lena: hmm meds are sensitive, Priya is nodding, right Priya?
[01:34] Dr. Priya: yes, especially false positives where the system suggests medication changes. We want very high precision for med recommendations, recall can be higher in downstream review but not at the triage suggestion level, otherwise clinicians get alarm fatigue.
[01:50] Samir: understood — so action: tighten threshold for medication NER guardrail and increase weight in the scoring for med-entity precision. Rosa you suggested weight 2x?
[01:59] Rosa: yep we proposed doubling negative-sample weight for med tokens for the score, that drops the effective threshold for those flags.
[02:12] Evan: quick infra Q — are these metrics from hosted traffic or staging? I thought some of these came from the smoke-run we did yesterday that hit dedicated pool.
[02:21] Rosa: it's mixed; the primary eval was on a curated 1k sample from staging but we replayed a small slice of hosted logs; the transcript earlier mis-labeled a bunch as "K V cash" — it should be KV cache hits.
[02:35] Marcus: oh right I saw odd cache hit rates in the log — <crosstalk> could be sequence length distributions.
[02:42] Samir: on the rollback simulation, Rosa can you walk through the steps we ran? We simulated a model regression and triggered the fallback.
[02:49] Rosa: sure: step 1 we flipped the canary to a degraded quantized build v1.2-q4, step 2 we generated synthetic heavy-context prompts that historically cause hallucinations, step 3 we hit the anomaly detector (score delta > 0.15) which then routed traffic per policy to the fallback variant (v1.1). Logs show average lat increase +40ms during reroute but no error spikes.
[03:15] Speaker 2: hmm 40 ms is fine, but what's the token-cost delta? We need cost impact numbers for PM.
[03:22] Samir: cost delta was small; the quantized variant cost per token dropped a bit but the reroute keeps more requests on the higher-cost fallback temporarily — Rosa to share the cost delta in the sheet.
[03:32] Rosa: yep I'll add a column with cost per 1k tokens per variant and the estimated transient cost when canary fails.
[03:40] Lena: also, can we log the exact user query for any med-entity false positives? For compliance priya wants a record for audit.
[03:48] Dr. Priya: yes we need auditability and an exportable CSV with the original text, model output, confidence, and which guardrail fired. We also need to anonymize PHI fields.
[03:59] Evan: Agreed, SRE can run a script to redact patient names and emit salted hashes. I'll take that.
[04:06] Marcus: regarding routing — we had discussed dedicated routing for high-risk workflows. Any update?
[04:12] Samir: we recommend a hybrid: keep low-risk traffic on hosted for cost, route high-risk clinical flows to Dedicated with VPC for auditing and KMS integration. That gives you token-level logs plus stricter network controls.
[04:28] Lena: cost for Dedicated is a concern — we need predictable throughput SLAs. Can you put that in the pricing doc?
[04:33] Samir: yes I'll include estimated monthly commit ranges and an example SLA.
[04:38] Rosa: small note on prompts — pruning the prompt set removed 7 prompts that caused entity hallucinations. We replaced them with shorter templated prompts that include an instruction "do not invent medications".
[04:53] Speaker 3: will that reduce recall?
[04:56] Rosa: slight drop in recall for rare meds but precision increases materially; that's the tradeoff Priya asked for. We'll tune via the ensemble weighting.
[05:06] Dr. Priya: acceptable as long as there is manual review for low-confidence suggestions.
[05:11] Samir: let's walk the failure-mode simulation timeline we ran — Rosa?
[05:15] Rosa: timeline: at t=0 deploy degraded quant build to canary, at t+10m load increases, error rate for hallucination metric spikes, at t+11m automated policy triggers hook to route canary traffic to fallback, at t+14m we saw KPIs stabilize. We recorded traces for 95% of calls; a few traces had missing span ids due to sampling.
[05:38] Marcus: missing span ids — Evan can you look into trace sampling config?
[05:41] Evan: yep will check. Could be due to our trace agent config on the staging side.
[05:46] Speaker 1: there's a note about evaluation thresholds; what do you propose for FPR target on med-entities?
[05:51] Rosa: propose FPR <= 0.05 per-entity on production for med-entities, precision >= 0.92. For other general NER, relaxed to FPR <= 0.12.
[06:04] Lena: that seems strict but aligned with compliance. We'll need time to validate on live samples.
[06:09] Samir: agreement then — set med-entity FPR target 0.05, Rosa will add to scoring sheet.
[06:16] Rosa: done — I'll annotate rows. Also noted in the transcript: some words were transcribed as 'redwood console' turned into 'redwood counsel' — ignore that.
[06:26] Lena: ha, that would be a high-salary counsel.
[06:30] Marcus: question on guardrail rules — are they expression-based or model-output based? We discussed both.
[06:36] Rosa: both. There are deterministic guardrails (regex and allowlists) and detector-based guardrails (secondary classifier on outputs). For meds we use the detector + synonyms expansion.
[06:47] Dr. Priya: detector false positives worry me — what's the human-in-the-loop plan?
[06:51] Samir: Plan A: route high-risk to Dedicated with mandatory manual review for suggestions below 0.7 confidence. Plan B: for low-latency flows, rely on deterministic guardrails and sample audits.
[07:05] Lena: OK, and can we have an override audit trail? If clinician overrides suggestion, we log decision and reason.
[07:12] Evan: that's a product ask but doable — we'll add an "override" flag in the event payload.
[07:17] Speaker 2: any mention of competitors? I heard someone say Anthropic earlier — what's the context?
[07:21] Samir: just comparing our detection/rollback policy to Anthropic's safety toolkit; nothing urgent.
[07:28] Rosa: also flagged Cohere for embeddings speed, but irrelevant here.
[07:33] Marcus: ok pile of infra tasks — Marcus to add runbook items to confluence.
[07:38] Marcus: yes will do.
[07:41] Samir: quick live demo, Rosa you have the demo prompt set?
[07:44] Rosa: yeah I'll paste a short scenario — note: transcription may mangle the clinical terms.
[07:50] [08:00] Rosa: (pasted prompt) "Patient reports new onset dizziness after med X; recommend next step" — model suggests medication swap and flags med-entity M-123 with confidence 0.62. Guardrail flagged med-entity as low confidence -> route to review.
[08:22] Dr. Priya: output looks reasonable but confidence at 0.62 is low — we want manual review.
[08:28] Samir: threshold set to 0.7 for auto-suggest.
[08:31] Lena: we saw a false positive where the model invented a med code 'M-789' that doesn't exist.
[08:37] Rosa: that's the hallucination case. We added a detector to compare entities against a canonical med-list; if no match then flag as potential hallucination.
[08:48] Evan: canonical list update cadence? Weekly? Daily?
[08:52] Marcus: weekly update seems fine for now. We can add webhook for immediate updates.
[08:57] Speaker 1: are we keeping example logs in the shared drive? I recall a spreadsheet.
[09:01] Samir: yes Samir to upload latest sheet to the shared drive after the call.
[09:07] Rosa: another note: we saw a regression in long-context for followups; suggestion is to tweak KV cache eviction to retain user history for 3 turns for clinical flows. That improved context recall by ~6 points in our staging run.
[09:22] Marcus: but will that increase memory pressure on the Dedicated pool?
[09:26] Rosa: small increase; we measured GPU memory +0.8GB under typical batch sizes. Evan to validate on staging.
[09:33] Evan: will validate.
[09:36] Dr. Priya: anything else on safety?
[09:38] Lena: one last thing — audit log retention and export formats. We need at least 1 year retention and SOC2-ready export.
[09:46] Samir: Redwood can offer export and retention options; longer retention is an add-on. I'll include specifics in the follow-up.
[09:55] Speaker 2: can we summarize the new scoring change? I missed the exact formula.
[09:59] Rosa: short: original score = 0.5*precision + 0.5*recall; new med-weighted = 0.6*(precision_med) + 0.3*recall_med + 0.1*generic_score. I'll drop full formula in sheet.
[10:15] Lena: that's helpful.
[10:18] Samir: cool — actionable recap: 1) tighten med guardrail + update scoring; 2) run 2k eval; 3) rollback playbook run in staging; 4) privacy review of prompts.
[10:31] Rosa: I'll upload the annotated scoring sheet and include cost deltas and trace links.
[10:36] Marcus: timeline ok.
[10:38] Evan: I'll run the trace sampling fix and upload logs.
[10:41] Dr. Priya: Priya will provide signoff criteria for clinical safety.
[10:45] Samir: great — I'll send meeting notes and next steps. Next sync 2027-07-09 proposed.
[10:51] Lena: thanks team.
[10:54] Samir: thanks, we can drop off.

End of transcript.

References shared during call: scoring_spreadsheet_v2.xlsx (link in chat), rollback_playbook_draft.md (link), canonical_med_list.csv (link).

Notes on transcription: auto-transcript mis-heard 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' in several places; speaker labels sometimes generic (Speaker 1/2) where we inferred the speaker. Some punctuation and capitalization are imperfect.
